response.sql: WITH per_sex AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT sex, avg_acl_igg, avg_ana, avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM per_sex) AS ana_ratio FROM per_sex;

assumptions.assumption: The inner JOIN drops examinations with no matching patient. Each examination is one row and Patient.ID is the primary key, so each examination is counted once.
Patients with a NULL SEX form their own group. That group appears in the output and is included in the mean of per-sex averages.
The 'mean of the per-sex average ANA values' is the unweighted mean of the per-sex averages, not the mean over all examinations. A sex whose average ANA is NULL is excluded from that mean.
AVG ignores NULL values, as the request specifies. Averages are not rounded.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude patients with no recorded SEX, so only male and female groups are reported and the ratio denominator is the mean of those two groups.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_sex AS (SELECT p.SEX AS sex, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS avg_acl_igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT sex, avg_acl_igg, avg_ana, avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM per_sex) AS ana_ratio FROM per_sex;
